The shape of the market

Language work is bigger and broader than major names suggest.

Sorted by how many postings fall in each career sector. Translation and localization, computational, and editing skills are in especially high demand: those three sectors together account for about seven in ten postings.

Read by program

Linguistics Department programs, in job listing terms

A list of majors and minors ordered by number of jobs found that could readily be filled by those graduates. Includes some key words or roles used in ads and employers posting the most jobs relevant to each area. Postings can count toward more than one major or minor.

Editing & Publishing
Major · from manuscript to print and beyond
940 postings · median $70,646

A steady, well-defined profession. Editor, copyeditor, and proofreader roles are consistent and geographically spread, and academic publishers also hire heavily for journal work — peer review, research integrity, and editorial management — across the U.S. and internationally.

Common role wordseditor · writer · linguist · translator · proofreader · specialist
Employers in the dataWelocalize, Springer Nature, Elsevier, Wiley, SAGE
Computational Linguistics
Minor · where language meets machines
898 postings · median $98,629

The highest-paying path in the data by a clear margin. Localization, annotation, conversational-AI, and NLP roles dominate. Two kinds of jobs make up this count: many freelance localization and AI-training roles, and fewer, higher-paid engineering and research roles. The median reflects the second group more than the first.

Common role wordslinguist · engineer · specialist · translator · localization · manager
Employers in the dataWelocalize, Deepgram, Meridial, Welo Global, IQVIA

Earnings

The computing premium is the clearest signal

Median advertised salary by program. Computational Linguistics leads Linguistics by about $17,200, and the other three programs by about $27,800. Applied English Linguistics, Editing & Publishing, and TESOL sit within $900 of each other, so pay shouldn't be the deciding factor among them. Linguistics sits above those, helped by the many postings that call for multilingual or computational skills.

If you're a student, read this

Five things the data suggests

01

Localization/translation a big door (many can enter) — walk in with eyes open

The largest share of postings (19%), but heavily freelance and the lowest median pay of any major sector ($56,939). A fine first step; pair it with a specialization.

02

The computing minor is the earnings lever

Computational Linguistics leads every path on pay (median $98,629). Even a few programming and NLP courses move you toward it. Remember these medians span whole careers: senior titles outnumber entry-level ones nearly three to one.

03

Editing and TESOL are dependable professions

Consistent, broad demand with clear credentials — a Bachelor's plus style-guide fluency for editing, often a Master's for TESOL.

04

A second language pays

Specific languages are named constantly; Spanish and French lead, followed by Japanese, German, and Chinese. The language you already have is a marketable asset — name it.

05

Don't overlook government work

Federal language-analyst roles are a small slice (1% of postings) but well paid (median $91,360), and most students never think to search for them.

How to read this honestly

What this snapshot can and can't tell you

Read these limits before quoting a number

  • It's a snapshot, not a census. Postings open during one collection window, not a record of where graduates ended up.
  • The mix reflects where we searched. About two in three postings (64%) came through one commercial aggregator (Adzuna), which tilts the mix toward translation and localization vendors.
  • These are not starting salaries. The postings mix entry-level, mid-career, and senior positions (479 senior vs 189 entry-level by title), so each median reflects the whole career arc.
  • Salaries come from the ~60% of postings that stated one, which over-represents larger employers.
  • Remote-work share can't be read from this data — most postings leave location blank.
